newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Islamic militant killed by own bomb.
newsitem.headline: Islamic militant killed by own bomb.

text.p: An Islamic militant apparently preparing to launch a suicide attack against Israel was killed in the West Bank on Saturday when a bomb exploded prematurely in his hands, eyewitnesses said.
"After the bomb exploded, he was just in pieces, no one could have recognised him," said one witness in the town of Qabatya, near Jenin.
Jenin hospital officials confirmed the death of Hamas activist Mohammad Assaf, who officials had earlier identified as Assas.

Palestinian sources said late on Saturday PLO military intelligence forces arrested five Qabatya men known to have been Hamas activists with ties to Assaf. Palestinian officials declined to comment on the killing or the arrests.
The sources said Assaf was released from an Israeli prison two months ago, and had served numerous six-month jail sentences for Hamas activism.
Israeli security forces have been on high alert for weeks, fearing attempts by the Islamic Jihad guerrilla group to avenge the killing of the group's leader Fathi Shqaqi in Malta on October 26, 1995.
Shqaqi's attackers were never caught, but Israel is widely believed to have been responsible.
On occasion Hamas and Islamic Jihad have joined forces to carry out guerrilla operations against Israel.
The witnesses rejected statements by members of Assaf's family, who said the blast might have been caused by a mine planted by Israeli agents.
Israeli army and police officials said they were probing the circumstances of the explosions in the light of Assaf's record as a Hamas activist, but declined further comment.
Qabatya is in an area under joint control of Israeli and PLO security forces.
A wave of Islamic suicide bombings, following the assassination of a Hamas master bomb maker in Gaza, rocked the Jewish state in February and March, killing 59 people.
The bombings cost then-prime minister Shimon Peres a large lead in opinion polls and paved the way for his defeat by Benjamin Netanyahu in May elections.
They also prompted a PLO crackdown on Islamic militants.
Islamic Jihad's current leader said this week heavy security in Israel had hampered attempts to avenge Shqaqi's death, but it was waiting for the right moment to strike.
